chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Isma'il from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Safwan ibn Yahya from Mansur ibn Hazim from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he said:

Regarding a man who fasted during the middle of Sha'ban, then Ramadan caught up with him, he said: 'He fasts the month of Ramadan and restarts the fasting; if he fasted during the middle (of Sha'ban) and added one day to the half, he combines (the days) and fulfills the remainder of his obligation.'

Al-Sheikh (may Allah have mercy on him) said: 'If he became ill before he completed the first month with fasting, or after he completed it before he had fasted anything from the second, and he broke his fast due to illness, then in both cases he is not required to restart (from the beginning). That is indicated by what he narrated:'

key_terms.ظِهَارِ شَعْبَانَ: The middle of the month of Sha'ban

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for someone who started fasting in Sha'ban and continued through Ramadan?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the principle of 'building' (bina) upon voluntary fasts to fulfill the obligatory Ramadan fast, a key juristic concept in Shia fiqh. Al-Sheikh al-Tusi clarifies that illness does not reset the count, emphasizing continuity in worship, which aligns with the Shia view that voluntary acts can serve as valid foundations for obligatory duties when conditions permit.
